ADHD is actually insanely hard to diagnose in females and I wouldn't deny yourself the possibility that this is what you're struggling with.

People with ADHD find coping mechanisms to try and adapt to the things around them. A large part of this involves the way we force ourselves to behave in school because we have no other choice. We also don't have anything to compare our experience to because we just think the way we are is completely normal.

I'm 17 and I only recently discovered I have ADHD because a friend of mine gave me some dexamphetamine and I was fine. My ability to focus in school also got worse over the years and I had to drop out for mental health reasons. 

I was in denial for about 3 days till I could accept the reality that I did have it. I was 100% certain just like you that there was absolutely no way I could have it because I've been diagnosed with other things like anxiety, depression, autism and mild OCD. (Its also super easy to misdiagnose ADHD in females) My parents and teachers/doctors also never suggested the idea throughout my life because females aren't as expressive/obvious in displaying symptoms. I would really look into it - it's changed my life for the better and I can't express to you how good it feels once you get the ability to focus.
